title: Triple-product identity for the twisted lift
statement:
Fix $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$, and work over the group $\mathbb{Z}_k^n = (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n$ with primitive $k$-th root of unity $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. Given $j \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and a map $f \colon \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, let $F(x) = \omega_k^{\,j\cdot f(x)}$ be its $j$-twisted lift, and for $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$ let $\widehat{F}(s) = \mathbb{E}_x\!\big[F(x)\,\overline{\omega_k^{\,s\cdot x}}\big]$ be its Fourier coefficient, where $s\cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{E}$ denotes the uniform average over $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then the triple-product expectation over independent uniform $x,y$ equals a cubic sum of the Fourier coefficients:
\[
  \mathbb{E}_x\,\mathbb{E}_y\!\left[F(x+y)\,\overline{F(x)}\,\overline{F(y)}\right]
  = \sum_{s\in\mathbb{Z}_k^n} \bigl\lvert \widehat{F}(s)\bigr\rvert^2\,\overline{\widehat{F}(s)}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: F is the j-twisted lift ω_k^{j·f(x)}
expectations are uniform averages over ℤ_k^n in x and y independently
